fields.statement: Verifier at 92ba3601. Read the diff: a failing ship check (no --settled/--main) records red_head and red_checks (job ID or run ID or name, plus the attempt from the details URL) and leaves Head and Checks unset; --test-failures stays read-only; --settled --changed reports not settled while the head and check IDs/attempts match the recorded baseline, and its detail names the head, the failed checks and 'no failing test: an infra failure'; with no baseline it acts as --settled; --changed is refused without --settled. In the run engine a wait keeps the until command's last non-zero output and appends it to the timeout detail. ship-change.toml routes ci-triage on.fail to wait-ci-rerun (until 'rhiza ship check --settled --changed', 6h, max_visits 3, on.pass pr-green). RetryStep now picks the last-visited wait when two waits feed pr-green. Ran (RHIZA_* and GOTMPDIR unset, from a scratch worktree outside ~/code so the rootguard does not trip on the live daemon's usage.live.json): go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... ./internal/workflow/... gave ok (TestShipCheckFailed and TestShipCheckSettledChanged pass: baseline recorded, unchanged red head not settled and named, new job ID running not settled, then finished settled, newer attempt settled, new head settled, no baseline acts as --settled). go test -trimpath ./internal/run/... gave ok (TestWaitTimeoutDetailHoldsLastOutput: 'did not hold within 5s: <last output>'; Retry* tests pass). go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-ship-rerun-fail|run-ship-infra-wait|run-ship-ci-fix)' gave PASS for all three. run-ship-infra-wait drives ci-triage fail to wait-ci-rerun, which passes on a rerun to pr-green (visit 2) to signoff to end.
